claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy contains dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Sharp internal boundaries in the initial alloy are prone to microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile loading.
Microcracking at internal boundaries contributes to brittle tensile failure in the initial alloy.
Adding 1–2 at.% Nb and applying controlled slow cooling will cause Nb to segregate to lamellar boundaries.
Adding 1–2 at.% Nb and applying controlled slow cooling will form Nb-rich nanoprecipitates at lamellar boundaries.
The resulting Nb-rich nanoprecipitates will be nanoscale and coherent with the surrounding phases.
The Nb-rich nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed along interphase or lamellar-colony boundaries.
Coherent Nb-rich nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the nanoprecipitates will increase strength through precipitation hardening.
Nb-rich nanoprecipitates at the boundaries will blunt potential crack tips.
Crack-tip blunting will reduce local stress concentrations.
Reduced local stress concentrations will suppress microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
The Nb-modified alloy will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength than the unmodified lamellar baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will have greater room-temperature elongation to failure than the unmodified lamellar baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will exhibit less microcrack formation and propagation than the unmodified baseline.
Keeping Nb within 1–2 at.% will avoid excessive formation of brittle Nb-rich phases.
The cooling schedule must prevent precipitate coarsening and undesirable phase transformations for the intervention to work.
The proposed strengthening and ductilization mechanism applies under room-temperature tensile conditions.
